GO:0005576.name: extracellular region

definition.text: The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

GO:0005576.comment: Note that this term is intended to annotate gene products that are not attached to the cell surface. For gene products at the cell surface, consider annotating to external side of plasma membrane ; GO:0009897.

definition.text: A motor activity that generates movement along a microtubule toward the minus end, driven by ATP hydrolysis.
Binding to a heavy chain of the dynein complex.
Binding to an intermediate chain of the dynein complex.
Binding to a light chain of the dynein complex.

GO:0005868.name: cytoplasmic dynein complex

definition.text: Any dynein complex with a homodimeric dynein heavy chain core that catalyzes movement along a microtubule. Cytoplasmic dynein complexes participate in many cytoplasmic transport activities in eukaryotes, such as mRNA localization, intermediate filament transport, nuclear envelope breakdown, apoptosis, transport of centrosomal proteins, mitotic spindle assembly, virus transport, kinetochore functions, and movement of signaling and spindle checkpoint proteins. Some complexes participate in intraflagellar transport. Subunits associated with the dynein heavy chain mediate association between dynein heavy chain and cargoes, and may include light chains and light intermediate chains.

GO:0005868.comment: Note that this term is labelled based on phylogenetic classification and community usage, rather than strict cellular localization. Cytoplasmic dynein complexes may contain ciliary dyneins; therefore the term is not linked to 'cytoplasm'. Cytoplasmic dynein complexes do not contain axonemal dyneins; see GO:0005858 axonemal dynein complex.

definition.text: A structure comprised of a core structure (in most organisms, a pair of centrioles) and peripheral material from which a microtubule-based structure, such as a spindle apparatus, is organized. Centrosomes occur close to the nucleus during interphase in many eukaryotic cells, though in animal cells it changes continually during the cell-division cycle.
Binding to a protein.

GO:0005929.name: cilium

definition.text: A specialized eukaryotic organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface and of some cytoplasmic parts. Each cilium is largely bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic (plasma) membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored to a basal body.

GO:0005929.comment: Note that we deem cilium and microtubule-based flagellum to be equivalent. In most eukaryotic species, intracellular sub-components of the cilium, such as the ciliary base and rootlet, are located near the plasma membrane. In Diplomonads such as Giardia, instead, the same ciliary parts are located further intracellularly. Also, 'cilium' may be used when axonemal structure and/or motility are unknown, or when axonemal structure is unusual. For all other cases, please refer to children of 'cilium'. Finally, note that any role of ciliary proteins in sensory events should be captured by annotating to relevant biological process terms.

GO:0042073.name: intraciliary transport

definition.text: The bidirectional movement of large protein complexes along microtubules within a cilium, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0042073.comment: Note that we deem cilium and microtubule-based flagellum to be equivalent.

synonyms.name: intraflagellar transport involved in cilium organization
intraflagellar transport involved in microtubule-based flagellum organisation

definition.text: Any of several large complexes that contain two or three dynein heavy chains and several light chains, and have microtubule motor activity.
The nucleus of a male germ cell, a reproductive cell in males.

GO:0035721.name: intraciliary retrograde transport

definition.text: The directed movement of large protein complexes along microtubules from the tip of a cilium (also called flagellum) toward the cell body, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0035721.comment: Note that we deem cilium and microtubule-based flagellum to be equivalent.

GO:0060271.name: cilium assembly

definition.text: The assembly of a cilium, a specialized eukaryotic organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface. Each cilium is bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored basally in a centriole.

GO:0060271.comment: Note that we deem cilium and microtubule-based flagellum to be equivalent.

definition.text: Either of the ends of a spindle, where spindle microtubules are organized; usually contains a microtubule organizing center and accessory molecules, spindle microtubules and astral microtubules.

A microtubule organizing center found in interphase cells, which organize a longitudinal array of three to five MT bundles from the nuclear envelope during interphase. Each MT bundle is composed of two to seven MTs arranged in an antiparallel configuration, with the dynamic MT plus ends extending toward the cell tips and stable minus ends near the nucleus.

GO:0097542.name: ciliary tip

definition.text: Part of the cilium where the axoneme ends. The ciliary tip has been implicated in ciliary assembly and disassembly, as well as signal transduction.

GO:0097542.comment: Note that cilia and eukaryotic flagella are deemed to be equivalent.

GO:0097546.name: ciliary base

definition.text: Area of the cilium (also called flagellum) where the basal body and the axoneme are anchored to the plasma membrane. The ciliary base encompasses the distal part of the basal body, transition fibers and transition zone and is structurally and functionally very distinct from the rest of the cilium. In this area proteins are sorted and filtered before entering the cilium, and many ciliary proteins localize specifically to this area.

GO:0097546.comment: Due to resolution issues, researchers are often unable to assign protein localization to more specific ciliary compartments such as the basal body, transition fibers or transition zone, and instead refer to 'ciliary base'. The terms GO:0036064 'ciliary basal body', GO:0097539 'ciliary transition fiber' and GO:0035869 'ciliary transition zone' represent strictly defined compartments at the ciliary base and should be used for annotation whenever possible. Also, note that cilia and eukaryotic flagella are deemed to be equivalent.

definition.text: A network of small fibers that surrounds the centrioles in cells; contains the microtubule nucleating activity of the centrosome.
The process in which the anatomical structures of the skeleton are generated and organized during the embryonic phase.
Binding to a chaperone protein, a class of proteins that bind to nascent or unfolded polypeptides and ensure correct folding or transport.

GO:0005930.name: axoneme

definition.text: The bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of cilia (also called flagella) in eukaryotic cells and is responsible for their movements.

GO:0005930.comment: Note that cilia and eukaryotic flagella are deemed to be equivalent. In diplomonad species, such as Giardia, the axoneme may extend intracellularly up to 5um away from the plane of the plasma membrane.

definition.text: Binding to a light intermediate chain of the dynein complex.
